name: Provide point-of-sale payment quotes to dealers
summary: Equipment dealers who offer the company's leases at the point of sale ask its vendor desk what a customer's monthly payment would be. About a third price themselves in the dealer portal; the rest phone or email a desk coordinator, who looks up the dealer's program and rate card, works out payments for several terms and end-of-term options and emails a quote. When the customer decides to finance, the coordinator collects the signed application and bureau consent, chases missing items and re-keys the application into the origination portal for credit. Speed matters because the dealer is often with the customer, and most delay comes from incomplete paperwork, exception approvals and the customer's own decision time.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 1,500 active dealers, a 13-person vendor desk in the Toronto area, a dealer portal with rate-card quoting and a CRM.
baseline.notes: Describes common practice: portal self-service quoting existed but many dealers still phoned or emailed, and paper or PDF applications were re-keyed by the desk.

trigger: A dealer phones, emails or uses the portal quote tool to ask for monthly payment options on equipment a customer wants.
end_state: The dealer has a payment quote and either the customer's signed application is submitted to credit, or the quote is delivered and not pursued, declined as outside the program, or referred for non-standard pricing.

volume.seasonality: Busier in spring and early autumn when construction, agricultural and trucking dealers sell most, and at dealers' month and quarter ends; about 15% lower in the second quarter of 2020.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation's process map: about two quote requests for every one of the roughly 1,850 vendor applications a month.

Org file cost (Job Bank NOC 64400 wage scaled to 2019-2022 and loaded x1.35). About 8 of the 12 coordinators' time goes to quoting and keying applications; the rest goes to communicating decisions and chasing status (other processes).
Supervisor spends about 40% of the week on rate exceptions, duplicate conflicts and quote spot checks; the rest on scheduling, coaching and reporting.
20 account managers each spend a few hours a month negotiating special terms and taking over large quotes; most of their time is dealer visits and training (other processes).

systems.name: Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)
Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)

steps.name: Dealer sends quote request
steps.description: A dealer salesperson who is with a customer asks for monthly payment options on a piece of equipment. The request comes by phone to the vendor desk line, by email to the shared desk mailbox, or through the quote tool in the dealer portal, with the equipment, price and sometimes the customer's name.

next.condition: dealer uses the portal quote tool
dealer phones or emails the desk

evidence.note: Channels are described in the sources; the 35% portal share is a tier C estimate for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Portal prices quote from loaded rate card
steps.description: The portal looks up the dealer's program, multiplies the equipment cost by the rate factor for each term and end-of-term option and shows the payments with taxes and fees. Requests outside the loaded card, such as used equipment past the age limit or an amount above the program cap, are pushed to the desk queue instead.

error.defect_description: An out-of-date rate card is still loaded after a rate change.

next.condition: dealer takes the printed quote to the customer and the desk does no more work on it
customer decides and the dealer sends the application to the desk
request falls outside the loaded rate card

evidence.note: Rate factor pricing and portal quoting are described; branch shares are tier C estimates.

steps.name: Pick up and log the request
steps.description: A vendor desk coordinator answers the call or takes the next email from the shared mailbox, opens a quote record in the origination portal under the dealer's code and notes the equipment, price, customer and what the dealer asked for. Emails that arrive late in the day wait until the next morning.

error.defect_description: Request logged under the wrong dealer code, so the wrong program is applied.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; about half of requests are live calls with no wait and the rest wait in the mailbox.

steps.name: Look up dealer program and rate card
steps.description: The coordinator opens the dealer's account in the CRM and the portal to find which program and rate card apply, any manufacturer promotion or rate buy-down in force, the documentation fee, allowed terms and end-of-term options. Dealers on older programs often have a card that differs from the standard one.

error.defect_description: Expired promotion or superseded rate card used.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Dealer-specific rate schedules are described; times are tier C.

steps.name: Check customer history and pick rate tier
steps.description: The coordinator searches the lease management system for the customer's existing contracts and payment record and asks the dealer how long the business has operated. From this the coordinator picks the rate tier to quote or marks the quote as subject to credit approval, and notes anything missing to price it.

error.defect_description: Quoted at a tier the customer will not qualify for, which leads to a re-priced approval.

next.condition: enough detail to price
equipment year, condition, province or down payment missing

evidence.note: Quotes shown as estimates subject to credit are described; the tier pick and 25% missing-detail share are tier C.

steps.name: Ask dealer for missing details
steps.description: The coordinator phones or emails the dealer for the facts needed to price the deal, typically the equipment year and hours for used units, the customer's province for sales tax, any trade-in or down payment and whether the customer wants a buyout or fair market value lease.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; a short call or email.

steps.name: Dealer supplies missing details
steps.description: The dealer salesperson goes back to the customer or to the equipment file and replies with the missing facts. Replies are fast when the customer is still on the lot and can take a day when the salesperson is on the road; some requests are simply dropped.

next.condition: details received
dealer does not reply or customer walks away

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; reply times range from minutes to most of a day.

steps.name: Check equipment eligibility and program limits
steps.description: The coordinator compares the request with the program: eligible equipment types, maximum age of used units, the dollar cap for application-only deals, minimum and maximum terms and any restricted industries. Most requests fit; others need a rate or structure exception, a hand-off to the account manager for a large deal, or a polite decline.

error.defect_description: An ineligible asset is quoted as standard.

control.basis: Vendor program terms: eligible equipment, used-equipment age, application-only dollar limits and term limits set by the director of vendor programs

next.condition: fits the program
needs a rate or structure exception
large or strategic deal for the account manager
equipment or customer type outside the program

evidence.note: Application-only dollar limits are documented; branch shares are tier C.

steps.name: Supervisor approves rate or structure exception
steps.description: The vendor desk supervisor reviews requests for a rate below the card, a longer term on used equipment, skip or seasonal payments or a deferred first payment. The supervisor approves within the small discretion band the pricing team allows, refuses and quotes standard terms, or passes larger concessions to the dealer's account manager.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: desk supervisor discretion band below the rate card, set by sales operations and pricing

next.condition: approved or quoted at standard terms
concession beyond the desk band

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; the supervisor is often on the phones and approvals wait from minutes to a few hours.

steps.name: Account manager negotiates special terms or large deal
steps.description: The dealer's account manager, usually in the field, calls the dealer to understand the competitive situation, decides whether a manufacturer or dealer rate buy-down can close the gap and either confirms special terms for the desk to quote or sends the deal to the pricing desk as a non-standard request.
outputs: approved special terms or pricing referral

next.condition: special terms confirmed within program authority
deal sent to the pricing desk for non-standard pricing

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; account managers spend most of the day visiting dealers.

steps.name: Calculate payment options
steps.description: The coordinator uses the portal quote screen or the desk spreadsheet calculator to work out payments for two or three terms and for $1 buyout, 10% purchase option and fair market value structures, including the first and last payment in advance, the documentation fee and GST, HST, QST or PST for the customer's province.

error.defect_description: Wrong term, residual or provincial tax applied in the calculation.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Rate factor arithmetic, end-of-term options and first-and-last payments are described; times are tier C.

steps.name: Prepare and send quote to dealer
steps.description: The coordinator generates the quote document from the portal template or an email template, in French for Quebec dealers, states that payments are subject to credit approval and how long the rate holds, emails it to the dealer and records the quote and a follow-up task in the CRM.

error.defect_description: Quote sent to the wrong dealer contact or without the validity date.

next.condition: dealer comes back with the customer's decision
no reply and quote large enough to follow up
quote picked for the supervisor's quality sample
quote delivered and the dealer never comes back

evidence.note: Quotes as estimates subject to credit are documented; branch shares are tier C.

steps.name: Dealer returns with customer decision
steps.description: The dealer presents the payment options to the customer, who compares them with cash, a bank loan or another lessor's offer. When the customer chooses to finance, the dealer comes back to the desk with a signed application or asks for a revised quote with a different term, amount or down payment.

next.condition: customer chooses to apply
dealer asks for a revised quote

evidence.note: The vendor presents the payment with the equipment quote and the customer chooses; the decision time and requote share are tier C.

steps.name: Follow up open quote with dealer
steps.description: When the CRM task comes due a few days later, the coordinator calls or emails the dealer to ask whether the customer has decided, whether a competitor's offer needs matching and whether the quote should be revised. Most quotes followed up are found to be lost or still undecided.

next.condition: customer still interested
customer bought elsewhere, paid cash or did not buy

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; follow-up tasks are set three to five days out.

steps.name: Supervisor spot-checks quote
steps.description: For a small sample of quotes each week, the vendor desk supervisor re-runs the payment from the rate card and checks the program, promotion, tax and wording. Errors found are corrected and the dealer is sent a revised quote; patterns are raised in coaching.

control.basis: Vendor desk quality assurance: supervisor sample review of quotes

next.condition: error found and quote reissued
dealer comes back with the customer's decision
no reply and quote followed up
quote delivered and the dealer never comes back

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; sample checks run alongside the dealer's discussion with the customer.

steps.name: Receive signed application and consent
steps.description: The dealer emails, faxes or uploads the signed credit application, which carries the business's legal and operating names, address, business number, years in business, the owners' names and home addresses and their signed consent to credit bureau inquiries. The coordinator attaches it to the quote record.

control.basis: PIPEDA Schedule 1 Principle 4.3 (knowledge and consent): signed consent from the business and each guarantor before a credit report is pulled, with proof kept on file

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Consent before credit checks and the vendor-supplied application are documented; no anti-money laundering identification applied to non-bank lessors before April 2025; times are tier C.

steps.name: Check application for completeness
steps.description: The coordinator checks that every field credit needs is filled and legible, that each owner has signed the consent, that the equipment and price match the quote and that a supplier quote or invoice is attached. About a third of dealer-supplied applications are missing a signature, an owner's address or the legal name.
outputs: complete application or list of gaps

error.defect_description: A missing guarantor consent or wrong legal name is not noticed.

next.condition: complete
items missing

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; incomplete dealer paperwork is the most common delay on vendor desks.

steps.name: Chase dealer for missing items
steps.description: The coordinator emails or calls the dealer listing exactly what is missing, such as an owner's signature on the consent, a home address, the customer's legal name as registered or the supplier invoice, and sets a reminder to check again.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; one email or call per chase.

steps.name: Dealer obtains missing items from customer
steps.description: The dealer goes back to the customer for the missing signature or details, which can mean a visit or a courier when the owner is on a job site. The corrected pages come back by email, fax or portal upload, or the customer loses interest and the file is dropped.

next.condition: items returned and rechecked
customer does not return the items

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; returns range from an hour to three days.

steps.name: Search for existing customer and duplicate submissions
steps.description: Before keying, the coordinator searches the portal and lease system for the customer's legal name and phone number to find existing contracts and any application already submitted in the last few months by another dealer, a broker or a direct account executive.

error.defect_description: Duplicate missed because the name was spelled differently.

control.basis: Channel conflict rule in the dealer and broker program agreements: one open application per customer and equipment, first submitter keeps the deal

next.condition: no conflict
open application from another channel found

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; duplicate checks protect dealer and broker commissions.

steps.name: Supervisor resolves duplicate or channel conflict
steps.description: The supervisor compares the two submissions, checks which channel submitted first and whether the equipment is the same, and talks to the broker channel or the account executive. The application is merged into the existing file, withdrawn, or allowed to proceed as a separate deal.

next.condition: proceeds as a separate deal
merged into or withdrawn in favour of the existing application

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; conflicts need a call with another team.

steps.name: Key application into origination portal
steps.description: The coordinator types the application from the PDF or fax image into the portal's application screens: legal and operating names, address, business number, industry, years in business, each owner's name, address and date of birth, the equipment, cost, term, structure and dealer code.

error.defect_description: Typing error in a legal name, address or date of birth that later causes a bureau no-hit or mismatch.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Applications arriving by fax, email and portal and keyed into the lessor's system are described; times are tier C.

steps.name: Attach documents and submit to credit
steps.description: The coordinator uploads the signed application and consent, the supplier quote or invoice and the payment quote to the portal file, sets the channel and requested structure, and submits the file to the credit intake queue, which assigns an application number.

error.defect_description: Supplier quote or consent page not attached.

next.condition: always

evidence.note: Submission returns an application number used to track status; times are tier C.

steps.name: Confirm submission to dealer
steps.description: The coordinator emails or calls the dealer with the application number and the usual time to a credit answer, and updates the CRM so the account manager can see the dealer's pipeline.

next.condition: application in the credit queue

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of vendor finance desks; a short confirmation.

exceptions.name: Rate or structure exception
exceptions.description: The dealer asks for a rate below the card, a longer term on used equipment or seasonal payments; the supervisor decides within a small band and passes bigger concessions to the account manager.

exceptions.name: Large or strategic deal referred
exceptions.description: Deals above the program cap or in a competitive fight go to the account manager, who either confirms special terms or sends the deal to the pricing desk.

exceptions.name: Incomplete application
exceptions.description: The signed application lacks an owner's consent signature, a home address or the legal name, and the desk chases the dealer, sometimes more than once.

exceptions.name: Revised quote
exceptions.description: The customer wants a different term, amount or down payment and the coordinator recalculates and resends the quote.

exceptions.name: Duplicate submission from another channel
exceptions.description: The same customer and equipment is already in credit from a broker or another dealer and the supervisor resolves who keeps the deal.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from quote request to the last desk action (quote delivered, or application submitted to credit)
benchmarks.population: Vendor desks of Canadian independent small-ticket lessors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Portal quotes are instant and most desk quotes go out within one to two hours. Because about 40% of requests go on to a revised quote, a follow-up or an application that takes days, the median case is a slower-than-typical quick quote, about two hours. The p90 reflects cases where the customer takes days to decide and the application has to be chased. No published figure was found.

benchmarks.unit: elapsed time for a dealer to generate a quote in a lender's dealer portal
benchmarks.population: A Canadian bank's equipment finance dealer portal (current)

evidence.note: Marketing statement; the 2019-2022 portals of mid-size independents were slower and covered fewer programs.

benchmarks.population: US small-ticket lessor working through dealers

evidence.note: Stated typical time to notify the dealer of an approval; sets the dealer's expectation the desk quotes in step s24.

benchmarks.population: A Canadian leasing broker network's vendor program

evidence.note: Program limits of this kind decide which quotes the desk can treat as standard in step s08.

benchmarks.population: US small-ticket lessor working through dealers, 2019

evidence.note: Approvals typically valid for up to 90 days; quotes are held for a shorter period.
Organisation file estimate.

pain_points.description: Signed applications from dealers are often missing an owner's consent signature, home address or the legal name, and the desk spends time chasing while the customer cools off.

evidence.note: Common complaint on vendor desks; about a third of dealer applications need a chase in this model.

pain_points.description: Applications that arrive as PDFs or faxes are re-typed field by field into the portal, which adds about ten minutes a file and introduces typing errors that surface later as bureau no-hits.

evidence.note: Fax, email and phone submissions alongside portals are documented; error rates are tier C.

pain_points.description: Dealers on older programs have their own rate cards and promotions, so coordinators look up the card for every quote and occasionally quote an expired rate.

evidence.note: Dealer-specific rate schedules are documented; the error rate is tier C.

pain_points.description: Rate exceptions wait for the supervisor or a field-based account manager while a competitor may be quoting the same customer.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file describes the same delay for the pricing desk.

pain_points.description: Emails that arrive in the late afternoon or evening wait until the next morning even though the dealer is with the customer.

evidence.note: Desk hours are business hours in the Toronto area while western dealers sell later.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.supports: A small-ticket lessor working through equipment dealers lets them submit applications by fax, phone, internet, mail, e-mail or web portal; credit approvals are typically valid for up to 90 days; about 55% of new applications were auto-decisioned in 2019; analysts usually decide within two hours for deals under $50,000.

sources.title: EasyLease: equipment and vendor leasing
sources.supports: Canadian vendor leasing: the vendor offers a monthly lease payment with its equipment quote, then gives the customer a lease application to sign; quick turnaround of 24 to 48 hours; application-only limits of $70,000 under two years in business and financial statements from $80,000.

sources.title: Technology financing pricing
sources.supports: Dealers receive a rate schedule by term, lease type and transaction size; payment equals the rate factor times equipment cost; terms of 12 to 60 months; $1 buyout carries higher rates than fair market value; the customer's credit check does not change the rate, only whether the deal is underwritten.

sources.title: Common questions answered on the AgentDealer integration with GreatAmerica
sources.supports: Dealer reps build financing quotes from lessor rate data updated daily and submit credit applications that return an application number used for status tracking.

sources.title: Pros and cons of vendor financing for equipment purchases
sources.supports: Vendor financing is arranged at the point of sale through manufacturer captives or third-party lessors; vendor leases typically ask for a first and last monthly payment at signing; used and specialised equipment carries higher rates.

sources.title: Partner with National Bank (equipment finance for dealers)
sources.supports: A Canadian lender's dealer portal lets dealers generate quotes in seconds, view and download quotes and apply for new financing.

sources.title: Offer equipment financing to your customers
sources.supports: Point-of-sale payment estimates are subject to credit approval; one application covers $10,000 to $500,000 on 24 to 72 month terms; no financial statements up to $250,000; same-day decisions.

sources.title: Applying for financing (help centre)
sources.supports: Calculator quotes assume an average credit rating and the final payment can differ after application; applications are completed online or in special cases phoned or faxed; approval typically notified to the dealer after 2 to 4 business hours.

sources.title: Wages for financial customer service representatives (NOC 64400)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $22.00, high $30.39; Quebec median $24.04 (2023-2024).

sources.title: PIPEDA Report of Findings #2015-005: dealer ran credit checks without consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Under PIPEDA Principle 4.3 an organisation should obtain separate consent for each hard credit inquiry and retain proof of consent for an appropriate period.

sources.title: PIPEDA case summary 2003-117: bank requires credit check on small business account applicant
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: A personal credit check on the individual behind a small business is a legitimate requirement when credit risk is involved, with the individual's consent.

sources.title: Equipment financing: end or cancellation of a lease
sources.supports: End-of-lease options include buying at fair market value or the stated purchase option, renewing, returning or trading up on approved credit.

sources.title: Vendor and broker financing
sources.supports: A Canadian lessor's vendor programs promise quick approvals and payments through simplified applications and offer customers end-of-term options and low down payments.

sources.title: Anti-money laundering obligations for factors, cheque cashers and financing/leasing entities
sources.supports: Financing and leasing entities became reporting entities under the PCMLTFA only as of April 1, 2025, so no federal AML identification duty applied to non-bank lessors in 2019-2022.

assumptions: Only quote requests that reach the lessor are counted (3,600 a month). Dealers who price from a printed rate card without contacting the lessor are outside the process.

About 35% of requests use the portal quote tool and 72% of those end with the printed quote and no desk work. Dealers who then submit the application themselves through the portal go straight to credit intake (the organisation file's equipment_vendor link) and are not counted as an outcome here.

The triggered_by links from manage-vendor-programs-and-rates (program terms) and manage-system-changes (system releases) are standing inputs that change how quotes are priced; they do not start cases, so their share is 0.

Organisation file gap: the price-non-standard-deals description says the vendor desk sends deals outside the rate card to the deal desk, but the process map has no link from quote-point-of-sale-payments to price-non-standard-deals. This workflow adds that output (outcome referred_to_deal_desk) and the organisation file was not changed.

Non-bank lessors were not reporting entities under Canada's anti-money laundering law until April 1, 2025, so the desk does no AML identification; identity checks happen later in credit intake for credit and fraud reasons.
Bureau consent is collected on the signed application and is treated as a legal requirement under PIPEDA; Quebec dealers also receive French-language quotes and forms.

Cycle time ends at the last desk action. For quotes that are never pursued that is the moment the quote is sent, so the median is about an hour while cases that go on to an application take days because of the customer's decision time.
Staffing: 8 of the 12 coordinators' time is on this process; the remaining time goes to communicating credit decisions and status calls in the communicate-credit-decisions process.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
